transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

When I’m stressed after work and classes, I end up eating way more food in one sitting than seems normal for anyone. It's just gotten really out of hand lately, and I knew I needed to talk to someone about it.
After these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you ever do things to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of those things. I've never made myself throw up, fasted, or tried to exercise excessively after it happens. Instead, I just end up feeling incredibly drained and ashamed of myself.
How often do these episodes of eating large amounts of food occur, and for how many months has this been happening?
This has been happening at least once a week for about four months now. It all started back then when my workload at my job and my college classes both suddenly ramped up at the same time.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much faster than normal, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or eating even when you aren't actually hungry?

I definitely eat until I'm painfully full, to the point where my stomach is so bloated that it actually hurts to sit up. I also eat when I'm not hungry at all, just out of stress, but I'm not really sure if I eat faster than normal since I don't pay much attention to the speed.
During these episodes, do you feel a sense of loss of control, as if you can't stop eating or control how much you are eating?

Yes, absolutely. Once I start, it's like a switch flips in my brain and I'm telling myself to stop because I'll feel sick, but my hand is just on autopilot. I keep reaching for the food and feel like I just can't make myself stop.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets all the diagnostic criteria for Binge Eating Disorder (ICD-10: F50.8), including recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food with a sense of lack of control, eating until uncomfortably full, eating when not hungry, and experiencing marked distress (shame, feeling drained) afterward, occurring at least once a week for four months. Compensatory behaviors (purging, fasting, excessive exercise) have been ruled out, which excludes Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). Therefore, the diagnosis of F50.8 is confirmed.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Binge Eating Disorder (classified under F50.8, Other eating disorders). She describes recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by eating unusually large amounts of food accompanied by a subjective sense of loss of control. These episodes are associated with eating until uncomfortably full, eating when not physically hungry, and feeling intense shame and distress afterward. The episodes have occurred at least once a week for four months. The absence of recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors (such as self-induced vomiting, fasting, or excessive exercise) rules out Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2).
